explanation_en: This idiomatic expression refers to unethical, underhanded, or illegal actions performed to achieve a goal, often on behalf of someone else who wants to keep their hands clean. It is used in political, corporate, and everyday contexts to describe sabotage, smear campaigns, or unpleasant tasks.

examples.en_text: The boss always asks Juan to do the dirty work because he knows he won't complain.
examples.target_text: El jefe siempre le pide a Juan que haga el trabajo sucio porque sabe que no se quejará.

examples.en_text: I don't want to participate in their political campaigns; there is always someone who has to do the dirty work.
examples.target_text: No quiero participar en sus campañas políticas; siempre hay alguien que tiene que hacer el trabajo sucio.

examples.en_text: In this group project, I had to do the dirty work of checking all the boring data.
examples.target_text: En este proyecto de grupo, a mí me tocó hacer el trabajo sucio de revisar todos los datos aburridos.

examples.en_text: The politician hired a private detective to do the dirty work for him.
examples.target_text: El político contrató a un detective privado para que hiciera el trabajo sucio por él.

examples.en_text: You always leave me the dirty work of cleaning the kitchen after the party.
examples.target_text: Siempre me dejas el trabajo sucio de limpiar la cocina después de la fiesta.

examples.en_text: If you want to fire those employees, do it yourself; I am not going to do your dirty work.
examples.target_text: Si quieres despedir a esos empleados, hazlo tú mismo; yo no voy a hacer tu trabajo sucio.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'truce,' in everyday Spanish 'dar una tregua' or having 'días de tregua' refers to a temporary relief, respite, or break from something unpleasant, like bad weather, work, or illness. It is widely used in news reports and casual conversations to describe a pause in difficult conditions.

examples.en_text: The heat is giving us no respite this summer; the thermometers don't drop below forty degrees.
examples.target_text: El calor no nos da tregua este verano; los termómetros no bajan de los cuarenta grados.

examples.en_text: I've been working non-stop for weeks and my body is already asking for a break.
examples.target_text: Llevo semanas trabajando sin parar y mi cuerpo ya me pide una tregua.

examples.en_text: The two countries agreed on a twenty-four-hour truce to allow humanitarian aid.
examples.target_text: Los dos países acordaron una tregua de veinticuatro horas para permitir la ayuda humanitaria.

examples.en_text: Finally, the cough gave me a break and I was able to sleep all night.
examples.target_text: Por fin la tos me dio una tregua y pude dormir toda la noche.

examples.en_text: Let's make a truce and not talk about politics during Christmas dinner.
examples.target_text: Hagamos una tregua y no hablemos de política durante la cena de Navidad.

examples.en_text: Between classes, work, and the gym, my schedule gives me no respite.
examples.target_text: Entre las clases, el trabajo y el gimnasio, mi agenda no me da tregua.

explanation_en: Used to indicate that something possesses a quality inherently or by its very nature, without needing external factors. It translates to 'in itself' or 'inherently.' It is a very common adverbial phrase in both spoken and written Spanish.

examples.en_text: The exam in itself is quite difficult, so don't get any more nervous.
examples.target_text: El examen de por sí es bastante difícil, así que no te pongas más nervioso.

examples.en_text: Traveling in winter by itself has its risks, but with this storm it's worse.
examples.target_text: Viajar en invierno de por sí tiene sus riesgos, pero con esta tormenta es peor.

examples.en_text: This dish is already quite spicy in itself, there's no need to add more sauce.
examples.target_text: Este plato de por sí es bastante picante, no hace falta que le eches más salsa.

examples.en_text: She is inherently a very shy person, which is why she doesn't speak much in meetings.
examples.target_text: Ella de por sí es una persona muy tímida, por eso no habla mucho en las reuniones.

examples.en_text: Renting an apartment downtown is already expensive in itself, and the electricity bills make it even worse.
examples.target_text: Alquilar un piso en el centro de por sí es caro, y los gastos de luz lo hacen aún peor.

examples.en_text: The new program is slow by itself, but with so many open files it doesn't work.
examples.target_text: El nuevo programa de por sí es lento, pero con tantos archivos abiertos no funciona.

explanation_en: A versatile prepositional verb meaning to seize, obtain, master, or gain control of something. In the context of fires, 'hacerse con el fuego' means to get it under control. It can also mean to buy or acquire something in other contexts.

examples.en_text: At first, the new design software was difficult, but I've already mastered it.
examples.target_text: Al principio el nuevo programa de diseño era difícil, pero ya me he hecho con él.

examples.en_text: The teacher had trouble at the beginning of the class, but soon managed to get the situation under control.
examples.target_text: El profesor tuvo problemas al principio de la clase, pero pronto logró hacerse con la situación.

examples.en_text: It took me a few weeks to get the hang of the new car because it was automatic.
examples.target_text: Tardé unas semanas en hacerme con el coche nuevo porque era automático.

examples.en_text: The new manager has not yet managed to get the team under control.
examples.target_text: El nuevo director técnico todavía no ha logrado hacerse con el equipo.

examples.en_text: Although German is a difficult language, with constant practice you will master it.
examples.target_text: Aunque el alemán es un idioma difícil, con práctica constante te harás con él.

examples.en_text: I was very nervous before the presentation, but I took a deep breath and got my nerves under control.
examples.target_text: Estaba muy nervioso antes de la presentación, pero respiré hondo y me hice con los nervios.

explanation_en: This phrase means 'at this hour' or 'given how late/early it is.' It is used to emphasize that a certain state or action is remarkable, unfortunate, or unexpected given the current time of day.

examples.en_text: Are you really going to drink coffee at this hour? You won't be able to sleep.
examples.target_text: ¿De verdad vas a tomar café a la hora que es? No vas a poder dormir.

examples.en_text: I don't like people calling on the phone at this hour; it's almost midnight.
examples.target_text: No me gusta que la gente llame por teléfono a la hora que es; ya es casi medianoche.

examples.en_text: The children shouldn't be playing in the street at this hour.
examples.target_text: Los niños no deberían estar jugando en la calle a la hora que es.

examples.en_text: Are you still studying at this hour? You should go to bed.
examples.target_text: ¿Todavía estás estudiando a la hora que es? Deberías irte a la cama.

examples.en_text: It's hard to find an available bus at this hour; it's better to order a taxi.
examples.target_text: Es difícil encontrar un autobús libre a la hora que es, es mejor pedir un taxi.

examples.en_text: Tell your brother to turn off the TV; you can't make so much noise at this hour.
examples.target_text: Dile a tu hermano que apague la televisión, no se puede hacer tanto ruido a la hora que es.

explanation_en: Meaning 'from top to bottom' or 'thoroughly/completely.' It can describe looking at someone thoroughly, cleaning a place completely, or being covered in something (like sweat or mud) from head to toe.

examples.en_text: We had to clean the kitchen from top to bottom before the guests arrived.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que limpiar la cocina de arriba a abajo antes de que llegaran los invitados.

examples.en_text: The museum guard looked me up and down before letting me in.
examples.target_text: El guardia del museo me miró de arriba a abajo antes de dejarme entrar.

examples.en_text: I read the instruction manual from top to bottom, but I still don't understand how it works.
examples.target_text: Me leí el manual de instrucciones de arriba a abajo, pero sigo sin entender cómo funciona.

examples.en_text: I searched the whole house from top to bottom for the car keys, but I didn't find them.
examples.target_text: Busqué las llaves del coche por toda la casa de arriba a abajo, pero no las encontré.

examples.en_text: Since she has lived here her whole life, Laura knows the city inside out.
examples.target_text: Como ha vivido aquí toda su vida, Laura se conoce la ciudad de arriba a abajo.

examples.en_text: We decided to paint the living room from top to bottom to give it a more modern look.
examples.target_text: Decidimos pintar el salón de arriba a abajo para darle un aspecto más moderno.

explanation_en: A colloquial expression used when something is so bad, poorly done, or chaotic that there is no redeeming quality or logical starting point to fix it. It translates to 'there is no making sense of it' or 'it's a total mess.'

examples.en_text: I tried to watch the new movie, but the plot is so bad that there's no making sense of it.
examples.target_text: He intentado ver la nueva película, pero el argumento es tan malo que no hay por dónde cogerlo.

examples.en_text: His explanation about why he arrived late makes no sense at all; nobody believes it.
examples.target_text: Su explicación sobre por qué llegó tarde no hay por dónde cogerla; nadie se la cree.

examples.en_text: I've read the draft of your project and, honestly, there's no making sense of it. We have to start over.
examples.target_text: He leído el borrador de tu proyecto y, sinceramente, no hay por dónde cogerlo. Tenemos que empezar de nuevo.

examples.en_text: The argument he used in the debate has no logic, there's no making sense of it.
examples.target_text: El argumento que usó en el debate no tiene lógica, no hay por dónde cogerlo.

examples.en_text: This article you have written is full of contradictions, there's no making sense of it.
examples.target_text: Este artículo que has escrito está lleno de contradicciones, no hay por dónde cogerlo.

examples.en_text: The idea of opening a coat store in the desert makes absolutely no sense.
examples.target_text: La idea de abrir una tienda de abrigos en el desierto no hay por dónde cogerla.

explanation_en: The reflexive idiom 'quitarse de en medio' means to get out of the way, to withdraw, or to avoid being in a certain place or situation. In this context, it refers to finishing errands quickly to get out of the oppressive heat.

examples.en_text: The boss is coming in a bad mood, so it's better for us to get out of the way quickly.
examples.target_text: Viene el jefe de mal humor, así que es mejor quitarnos pronto del medio.

examples.en_text: I realized I was in the waiters' way and decided to get out of the way quickly.
examples.target_text: Me di cuenta de que molestaba a los camareros y decidí quitarme pronto del medio.

examples.en_text: When they saw the ambulance coming, the pedestrians had to get out of the way quickly.
examples.target_text: Cuando vieron venir la ambulancia, los peatones tuvieron que quitarse pronto del medio.

examples.en_text: If you are going to take the photo now, let me know so I can get out of the way quickly.
examples.target_text: Si vas a sacar la foto ahora, avísame para quitarme pronto del medio.

examples.en_text: We don't want to get in the way in the kitchen, so we are going to get out of the way quickly.
examples.target_text: No queremos estorbar en la cocina, así que vamos a quitarnos pronto del medio.

examples.en_text: As soon as the argument started, she preferred to get out of the way quickly to avoid trouble.
examples.target_text: En cuanto empezó la discusión, ella prefirió quitarse pronto del medio para evitar problemas.

explanation_en: The construction 'hace' + time indicator is used to express how long ago something happened. Using 'escasas' (scarce/few) instead of 'pocas' adds a touch of precision or emphasis, meaning 'barely' or 'just a few' hours ago. It is common in journalistic and formal spoken Spanish.

examples.en_text: The president announced his resignation just a few hours ago in a press conference.
examples.target_text: El presidente anunció su dimisión hace escasas horas en una rueda de prensa.

examples.en_text: We arrived in Madrid just a few hours ago and we are still a bit tired from the trip.
examples.target_text: Llegamos a Madrid hace escasas horas y todavía estamos un poco cansados del viaje.

examples.en_text: I sent you the final report just a few hours ago, let me know if you need any changes.
examples.target_text: Te envié el informe final hace escasas horas, avísame si necesitas algún cambio.

examples.en_text: The storm ended just a few hours ago and now the sky is completely clear.
examples.target_text: La tormenta terminó hace escasas horas y ahora el cielo está completamente despejado.

examples.en_text: I spoke with her just a few hours ago and she told me she wouldn't be able to come to the dinner.
examples.target_text: Hablé con ella hace escasas horas y me dijo que no podría venir a la cena.

examples.en_text: I bought the plane tickets just a few hours ago and they have already gone up in price.
examples.target_text: Compré los billetes de avión hace escasas horas y ya han subido de precio.

explanation_en: This prepositional phrase means 'according to', 'judging by', or 'in light of' something. It is a B2/C1 level expression frequently used in news reporting, legal contexts, and formal discussions. It is followed by a noun or a clause introduced by 'que'.

examples.en_text: Judging by the dark clouds, I think it's going to rain soon.
examples.target_text: A tenor de las nubes negras, creo que va a llover pronto.

examples.en_text: In light of the latest results, the company will have to change its strategy.
examples.target_text: A tenor de los últimos resultados, la empresa tendrá que cambiar de estrategia.

examples.en_text: Judging by what you told me, it seems that the exam was quite difficult.
examples.target_text: A tenor de lo que me has dicho, parece que el examen fue bastante difícil.

examples.en_text: According to the new hotel rules, pets are not allowed in the rooms.
examples.target_text: A tenor de las nuevas normas del hotel, no se permiten mascotas en las habitaciones.

examples.en_text: Judging by her smile, the news she received was very good.
examples.target_text: A tenor de su sonrisa, la noticia que recibió fue muy buena.

examples.en_text: In light of the rise in prices, we will have to reduce our expenses this month.
examples.target_text: A tenor de la subida de los precios, tendremos que reducir nuestros gastos este mes.

explanation_en: This phrase means to be at the absolute limit of one's capacity or on the verge of a critical state (usually negative, like collapse, exhaustion, or madness). It is widely used to describe both systems under extreme pressure and individuals experiencing high stress. It is a very common idiomatic collocation in both everyday and journalistic Spanish.

examples.en_text: The development team is working at the limit of their strength to finish the project.
examples.target_text: El equipo de desarrollo está trabajando al límite de sus fuerzas para terminar el proyecto.

examples.en_text: His selfish attitude has me at the limit of my patience.
examples.target_text: Su actitud egoísta me tiene al límite de mi paciencia.

examples.en_text: Many families live at the limit of their financial resources at the end of the month.
examples.target_text: Muchas familias viven al límite de sus recursos económicos a fin de mes.

examples.en_text: The athlete ran at the limit of his abilities to win the gold medal.
examples.target_text: El atleta corrió al límite de sus capacidades para ganar la medalla de oro.

examples.en_text: The computer's memory is at the limit of its capacity with so many open programs.
examples.target_text: La memoria del ordenador está al límite de su capacidad con tantos programas abiertos.

examples.en_text: Driving so fast in the rain is being on the verge of a serious accident.
examples.target_text: Conducir tan rápido en la lluvia es estar al límite de un accidente grave.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression means to be unable to handle a workload, demand, or situation because it is too overwhelming. It is extremely common in Spain and Latin America, used in both professional contexts (e.g., a business overwhelmed with orders) and everyday life. The verb 'dar' is conjugated according to the subject.

examples.en_text: The new waiter cannot cope with so many customers on the terrace.
examples.target_text: El camarero nuevo no da abasto con tantos clientes en la terraza.

examples.en_text: Delivery companies cannot keep up during the Christmas season.
examples.target_text: Las empresas de reparto no dan abasto durante la época de Navidad.

examples.en_text: Between work and university exams, I can't cope.
examples.target_text: Entre el trabajo y los exámenes de la universidad, no doy abasto.

examples.en_text: Yesterday at the shop we couldn't keep up with the sales.
examples.target_text: Ayer en la tienda no dábamos abasto con las rebajas.

examples.en_text: The server is old and can't handle so many visits to the website.
examples.target_text: El servidor es antiguo y no da abasto con tantas visitas a la web.

examples.en_text: The hospital doctors couldn't cope during the flu season.
examples.target_text: Los médicos del hospital no daban abasto durante la temporada de gripe.
